checks.statement: For products updated to the M3 Expressive system, segmented buttons are no longer recommended; use a connected button group instead, which has mostly the same functionality and an updated visual design.
checks.condition: When choosing a component for an M3 Expressive product.

sourceHistory.summary: Expressive notice withdraws recommendation for segmented buttons and points to connected button groups.

implementation.notes: Choosing between segmented buttons and connected button groups is a product component-selection policy; this package implements the segmented-button component.

checks.statement: M3 segmented buttons have fully rounded corners, 40dp container height, sentence-case labels, optional check icons for selected state, new color mappings compatible with dynamic color, and official single-select and multi-select variants; M2 called them toggle buttons.
checks.condition: When implementing M3 styling or migrating from M2.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison enumerates M3 shape, height, typography, selection indicator, colors, and naming changes.

evidence.result: Default height uses the 40dp space600 token, and selected icon/check replacement and dynamic component token bindings are present.

checks.statement: Use on-surface, outline, secondary-container, and on-secondary-container color roles for the segmented button color mapping.
checks.condition: When styling segmented buttons for light or dark schemes.

sourceHistory.summary: Color diagram caption names the four roles used for segmented buttons.

evidence.result: The segment style is bound through the generated per-component token variables for label, outline, state and container colors.

checks.statement: Support enabled, disabled, hovered, focused, and pressed states for unselected segments.
checks.condition: For unselected segmented button segments.

sourceHistory.summary: Unselected state list names five interaction states.

evidence.result: Disabled and focus-visible states are explicit, and pressed state has a state layer; hover and enabled appearance rely on shared button/state bindings not demonstrated by this local selector.

implementation.notes: The full hover-state rendering was not exercised.

checks.statement: Support selected, hovered-selected, focused-selected, and pressed-selected states.
checks.condition: For selected segmented button segments.

sourceHistory.summary: Selected state list names the selected and three selected interaction states.

evidence.result: Checked inputs switch icon/check visibility and focus/pressed styling is present, but selected-hover and selected-pressed combinations are not established by the inspected local rules.

implementation.notes: No browser check of combined selected interaction states.

checks.statement: Size the container dynamically to its labels and divide its width evenly among segments; use 40dp height, 1dp outline, centered labels, at least 12dp left/right padding, 8dp between elements, and 48dp target size.
checks.condition: When sizing and laying out a segmented button at the documented default density.

sourceHistory.summary: Measurements table specifies container and segment sizing, height, outline, alignment, padding, spacing, and target size.

evidence.result: Segments use equal 1fr columns in a max-content grid and a 40dp minimum container height; segment rules set centered content, 12dp inline padding, 8dp icon gap, and at least 48dp target height.

checks.statement: Density changes only the component height; each step down in density removes 4dp from the height.
checks.condition: When reducing segmented-button density for a space-constrained UI.

sourceHistory.summary: Density section states density affects height only and each step removes 4dp.

evidence.result: Density modifies only the segment-height expression in 4dp increments while the minimum target height remains 48dp.

checks.statement: Use segmented buttons for a simple set of two to five options to select, switch views, or sort; for more choices or complex choices, use another component such as chips.
checks.condition: When selecting a component for a small set of related options.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage guidance limits segmented buttons to simple choices and redirects larger or complex sets.

implementation.notes: Choice counts and whether options are simple enough for segmented buttons are product information-architecture decisions.

checks.statement: Use two to five clearly divided segments. Each segment may contain label text, an icon, or both; do not exceed five, and consider chips for more choices.
checks.condition: When defining the options in a segmented button.

sourceHistory.summary: Segments guidance specifies count, separation, content, and the five-segment limit.

implementation.notes: The reusable renderer accepts caller-provided segments; the three-item specimen does not constrain production option count or authoring/content policy.

checks.statement: Use fully rounded corners on the segmented-button container by default.
checks.condition: When styling the segmented-button container.

sourceHistory.summary: Container guidance specifies fully rounded default corners.

evidence.result: First and last segment corners use the mapped segmented-button shape at both inline ends.

checks.statement: Icons may label a segment by themselves or appear with text; an icon used alone must clearly communicate the option it represents.
checks.condition: When using icons in segmented-button labels.

sourceHistory.summary: Icon guidance allows icon-only or icon-plus-text labels and requires clear icon meaning when alone.

implementation.notes: Whether a product icon communicates its option is a content/design review; the example uses icon-plus-text labels.

checks.statement: Keep labels short, clear, and consistent in length and label type; do not allow labels to wrap. If text does not fit, consider using an icon alone, and avoid mixing icon-only labels with text labels across segments.
checks.condition: When segments use visible labels.

sourceHistory.summary: Label guidance specifies concise, consistent, single-line labels and consistent label type.

implementation.notes: Label wording, consistency and wrapping are content authoring decisions; the reusable component renders caller-provided labels.

checks.statement: Use single-select when one option must be selected from a set, to choose an option, switch views, or sort across up to five options.
checks.condition: When exactly one choice is required from the set.

sourceHistory.summary: Single-select guidance covers selecting one option, switching views, and sorting up to five options.

implementation.notes: Whether one choice is mandatory is a product selection-model decision, not decided by the reusable control.

checks.statement: Use multi-select for two to five options when selection is optional; users may select none, one, or multiple options, including all options.
checks.condition: When users can independently select multiple options.

sourceHistory.summary: Multi-select guidance specifies option count and permits any selected subset, including none or all.

implementation.notes: Whether none, one or several choices are allowed is a product selection-model decision, not decided by the reusable control.

checks.statement: Leave adequate margins between the segmented button and viewport or frame edges. On larger screens, constrain segment padding so the set does not span the full width or leave excessive space around labels; segmented buttons may also appear within components such as bottom sheets or full-screen dialogs.
checks.condition: When placing segmented buttons in a screen, pane, or container.

sourceHistory.summary: Placement guidance describes edge margins, large-screen width/padding limits, and allowed nested placement.

implementation.notes: Screen/pane placement and margins are caller layout decisions; the specimen only sizes the control to its content.

checks.statement: When a segment uses both an icon and label text, replace its icon with a checkmark when selected.
checks.condition: When a selected segment has both an icon and visible label text.

sourceHistory.summary: Behavior guidance specifies replacement of the icon with a checkmark on selection.

evidence.result: For icon-plus-label segments, checked inputs hide the original icon and expose the check glyph while preserving its grid slot.

checks.statement: Assistive-technology users must be able to navigate to and activate segmented buttons and understand what each selection does.
checks.condition: For accessible segmented buttons.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases list navigation, activation, and understandable selection outcomes.

evidence.result: Segments are labeled native radio/checkbox inputs inside clickable labels, providing keyboard focus and activation with the selection label.

checks.statement: Use Tab to navigate between buttons and arrow keys to move between segments. For single-select segments, Space or Enter selects or unselects the focused segment. For multi-select segments, Space or Enter selects an unselected segment, can select all segments, and can unselect a selected segment.
checks.condition: When operating segmented buttons with a keyboard.

sourceHistory.summary: Interaction guidance distinguishes keyboard behavior for single-select and multi-select variants.

evidence.location: Chromium baseline http://127.0.0.1:8081/md3/components/segmented-buttons?preview.compare=interactive; focus Home with locator, press Enter, inspect checked input values
evidence.result: On the single-select specimen, Enter left Home unchecked and Saved selected; the required Enter activation did not select the focused segment.

implementation.notes: Browser observation supplied by parent on the frozen baseline; native radio behavior matches the authored input implementation.

checks.statement: Give the outline at least 3:1 contrast against its background or surface. Show selection with both a checkmark and a color change so color is not the only indicator.
checks.condition: When rendering segmented-button boundaries and selected states.
checks.notes: The accessibility page explicitly requires both indicators; the overview describes the check icon as optional. The source does not reconcile this difference, so the related section remains unclear.

sourceHistory.summary: Contrast guidance sets the minimum outline contrast and requires a non-color selection indicator.

evidence.result: The selected state changes token-bound label/container colors and uses a check glyph, but this source inspection does not calculate the outline-to-surface contrast ratio.

implementation.notes: The 3:1 contrast threshold needs resolved rendered colors.

checks.statement: Place initial focus on the first segment, whether or not it is selected; in left-to-right languages this is the leftmost segment and in right-to-left languages the rightmost.
checks.condition: When segmented buttons receive initial focus.

sourceHistory.summary: Initial-focus guidance specifies first segment and language-direction-dependent side.

evidence.result: No code explicitly moves initial focus to the first segment; native radio tab behavior may focus the checked option instead.

implementation.notes: Requires runtime confirmation of initial focus in checked and unchecked configurations.

checks.statement: Use visible label text as the accessibility label. For icon-only segments, label the represented action. Expose single-select as a Radiogroup and multi-select options as Checkboxes.
checks.condition: When exposing segments and their selection model to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance defines text/icon labels and variant-specific accessibility roles.

evidence.result: Inputs expose radio/checkbox roles and visible label text, but their common wrapper uses role=group for both variants; single-select lacks the required Radiogroup role.
